fine_trace.note: The fuzzed input is decoded as a binary TCP message header. The messageTypeAndChunkType field (OPNF) dispatches into SecureChannel creation and the vulnerable deferred-cleanup path.
OPN chunk admitted; the first OPN creates a fresh SecureChannel via UA_SecureChannelManager_create (channelId=1, tokenId=1) and opens it with Service_OpenSecureChannel.

Follow-up MSG chunks (CreateSession, ActivateSession, CreateSubscription) create an activated session S1 attached to the channel and add subscription sub1 to S1, so that closing the session later re-queues work onto the work queue.
The CLO chunk closes the channel while the channel/session/subscription state is still live; the actual cleanup is deferred.

ALL SecureChannel cleanup (state=CLOSED update, connection detachment, session unlinking) is deferred into the delayed callback embedded in the channel_entry. UA_free(dc) on this node later frees the entire channel_entry.
The trailing MSG CloseSession removes S1, enqueueing its cleanup callback at the HEAD of the delayed queue (S1_cleanup before E1_cleanup), since the CLO was processed earlier.

First drain (UA_Server_run_shutdown -> UA_WorkQueue_cleanup). Processing S1_cleanup re-entrantly enqueues sub1->delayedFreePointers at the head; the next SIMPLEQ_REMOVE_HEAD pops that re-entrant node instead of E1_cleanup, so after E1_cleanup's callback runs, UA_free(dc) frees the channel_entry while the queue head still points at it.

Second drain (UA_Server_delete -> UA_WorkQueue_cleanup) iterates the delayed queue whose head is the channel_entry freed during the first drain; reading dc->next from the freed memory triggers the MSan use-of-uninitialized-value.
